```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's payer and buyer are the same solo founder, so one person makes the decision. A's buyer is an eng manager buying seats for a team. Both briefs frame the security and governance bar (SOC2, ZDR, SSO) as the likely purchase driver, which makes a 90-day close harder for A.",
    "B has a sourced, cheap channel that reaches its buyers directly: about $0.52 CPC from Indie Hackers newsletter sponsorships. A's only sourced paid channel costs about $650 per devtools SQL, and its Product Hunt launch costs $3,300–$6,000 in founder time. That is a poor fit for a solo operator chasing a first sale.",
    "B's solo buildability has some support: Tax Threshold Radar is a sourced, near-identical one-person product priced at $49/mo, though its traction is unverified. A's claim that a solo builder can ship in six weeks is explicitly marked [unsourced].",
    "Both ideas compete against free offerings. A's free competitor is Slack Code, bundled into every Slack plan, and A also faces at least five direct competitors. B's free monitors come from Kintsugi, Numeral, and TaxJar, but they are funnels into paid filing. That leaves room for a neutral, monitoring-only or MoR-decision wedge for founders who don't want a filing upsell.",
    "B's per-account price anchor ($29–49/mo per founder) sits above A's anchor ($8–10/seat from Lody), and B's first sale needs only one buyer's approval."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's demand case rests on an uncited YC Fall 2026 RFS and on 'several teams converged on this feature set.' Competitor convergence shows a crowded market, not willingness to pay. The two demand quotes describe visibility pain, not a buyer paying for a standalone tool. The six-week solo build claim that the rest of the case depends on is marked [unsourced].",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Both briefs show the core feature offered free by better-resourced competitors. B also has serious unresolved risks: its demand quotes date back to 2020, Merchant-of-Record migration removes the need, low-revenue founders may not pay, the threshold data creates liability, and Tax Threshold Radar's traction is unverified. B wins mainly because a single-decision-maker buyer and a cheap, sourced channel make a first paying customer within 90 days more plausible. Neither brief shows evidence of anyone actually paying."
}
```
